summary: A one-day marine science expedition for 35 students and 8 chaperones in Key Largo, combining REEF classroom learning, a lionfish dissection, and a kayak tour through the mangroves of a Florida state park.

days.title: Fish, Lionfish & Mangroves
days.theme: Learn how citizen scientists track reef fish, investigate an invasive species up close, then paddle through a mangrove forest.

blocks.title: Florida Keys Fish & Adaptations
blocks.description: At the REEF campus, students learn how REEF's citizen scientists identify and record the fish of the Florida Keys, and how those fish are adapted to life on the reef.

blocks.title: Invasive Species: Lionfish Lesson & Dissection
blocks.description: Students investigate invasive lionfish through a guided dissection, looking at anatomy and adaptations and learning why lionfish are a conservation challenge for Florida Keys reefs.

blocks.title: Lunch (on your own)
blocks.description: Lunch is not included in this proposal. Your group can bring lunch or pick up food nearby.

blocks.title: Mangrove Ecology & Kayak Tour
blocks.description: Students kayak through the mangroves of a Florida state park and learn how mangrove ecosystems shelter young fish and protect the coast. Park entrance fees and staff gratuity are included.

studentsWill: Learn how citizen scientists identify and record Florida Keys fish.
Investigate invasive lionfish through a guided dissection.
Explore a mangrove ecosystem by kayak.
